name: Independent-Kinetic Screened Preferred-Frame
claimed_mechanism: A khronon field u carries the preferred-frame response, while an auxiliary scalar chi carries the propagating MOND mode. A multiplier lambda imposes a first-order constraint that fixes the screened preferred-frame coefficient alpha to e^-y without fixing the chi kinetic term. The chi kinetic term is normalized by an independent constant, so the P7 collision is avoided: screening controls only the preferred-frame coupling, not the propagating-mode kinetic normalization.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field, low-acceleration limit the chi field reproduces the MOND interpolation through mu(y)=1-e^-y, giving a 1/r potential with a_0 scaling. The preferred-frame term is suppressed by e^-y in high-acceleration environments, so alpha approaches zero where screening is strong. The finite chi kinetic normalization remains O(1), yielding a well-defined propagating mode and no vanishing kinetic term in the screened regime.
inequivalence_argument: It is inequivalent to every dead class listed because it changes the canonical structure by adding an independent chi kinetic sector and a multiplier constraint that decouples the screened preferred-frame coefficient from the propagating-mode kinetic normalization. No dead class with a single auxiliary field or a screened coupling alone can reproduce this separation, since here the constraint fixes alpha while leaving the chi kinetic term free. The architecture is therefore structurally distinct from coefficient-tweak or single-sector screened preferred-frame variants, and it does not rescale G or alter the frozen mu(y).
